selected_evidence.snippet: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is one of the most commonly diagnosed genetic disorders.

assertion.name: Asthma
assertion.description: Asthma may overlap with CF pulmonary symptoms, especially wheeze and dyspnea, and can complicate interpretation of obstructive respiratory findings.
distinguishing_features: CF diagnosis requires evidence of CFTR dysfunction (e.g., sweat chloride and/or genotype), while isolated asthma does not.
CF-asthma overlap remains debated, so objective CFTR-focused testing is needed when symptoms overlap.

selected_evidence.snippet: Respiratory symptoms for both CF and asthma include cough, wheezing, and dyspnea.

assertion.name: CF Foundation Diagnostic Criteria (2017)
assertion.description: Consensus guidelines from the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation for establishing a diagnosis of CF in individuals from newborn to adult, requiring evidence of CFTR dysfunction via sweat chloride testing combined with clinical features or two disease-causing CFTR mutations.
assertion.scope: Diagnosis of cystic fibrosis in all age groups

criteria_sets.name: Diagnostic criteria for cystic fibrosis
criteria_sets.description: CF diagnosis requires clinical features consistent with CF in at least one organ system OR positive newborn screen, PLUS evidence of CFTR dysfunction demonstrated by elevated sweat chloride (>=60 mmol/L) or identification of two CF-causing CFTR mutations.

selected_evidence.snippet: It is recommended that diagnoses associated with CFTR mutations in all individuals, from newborn to adult, be established by evaluation of CFTR function with a sweat chloride test.

assertion.name: NCT03525444
assertion.description: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor in patients aged 12+ with cystic fibrosis heterozygous for F508del and a minimal-function CFTR mutation. This landmark trial led to FDA approval of Trikafta.

selected_evidence.snippet: Elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor was efficacious in patients with cystic fibrosis with Phe508del-minimal function genotypes, in whom previous CFTR modulator regimens were ineffective.

assertion.name: Orphanet Cystic fibrosis record
assertion.description: Orphanet structured record for cystic fibrosis, including synonyms, definition, inheritance, natural history, epidemiology, genes, HPO phenotypes, and cross-references.

assertion.name: Primary ciliary dyskinesia
assertion.description: Primary ciliary dyskinesia can closely resemble cystic fibrosis with chronic sinopulmonary symptoms driven by impaired mucociliary clearance.
distinguishing_features: CF is caused by CFTR dysfunction, whereas primary ciliary dyskinesia is caused by structural/functional ciliary defects.
PCD is generally less prevalent than CF and requires a different specialist diagnostic work-up and management strategy.

selected_evidence.snippet: Cystic fibrosis (CF) and Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) are both rare chronic diseases, inherited disorders associated with multiple complications, namely respiratory complications, due to impaired mucociliary clearance that affect severely patients' lives.

assertion.name: Sweat Chloride Test (Quantitative Pilocarpine Iontophoresis)
assertion.description: Gold standard diagnostic test for CF. Pilocarpine iontophoresis stimulates localized sweating; sweat is collected and chloride concentration measured. Chloride >=60 mmol/L is diagnostic, 30-59 mmol/L is intermediate, <30 mmol/L is CF-unlikely.
assertion.notes: Must be performed at a CF Foundation-accredited laboratory. Minimum sweat volume required for reliable results. Should be performed on two separate occasions.

selected_evidence.snippet: Even in 2016, the most reliable and widely available diagnostic test for CF is the measurement of chloride concentration in sweat.

value.prompt: Which airway epithelial and goblet-cell states causally maintain mucus overproduction and airway remodeling in asthma, and which states are reversible downstream consequences of type 2 inflammation?
value.rationale: The asthma entry captures type 2 signaling, mucus overproduction, and airway remodeling, but it does not yet distinguish reversible inflammatory epithelial states from remodeled mucous-cell states that continue after the trigger is removed. Recent human airway-epithelium perturbation data make this a tractable causal experiment rather than a descriptive subtype problem.

assertion.name: Patient-derived airway epithelium IL-13 withdrawal and MTOR-rescue assay
assertion.description: Culture patient-derived bronchial epithelial cells at air-liquid interface or in an airway chip, induce type 2 mucous metaplasia with IL-13, withdraw the cytokine, and test whether MTOR inhibition separates reversible mucus induction from persistent remodeling-associated epithelial states.

model_systems.name: Patient-derived bronchial air-liquid-interface epithelium
model_systems.description: Differentiated human airway epithelial culture preserving basal, ciliated, and mucus-producing epithelial states for controlled cytokine withdrawal and epithelial-state resolution assays.
model_systems.cell_source: primary bronchial epithelial cells from severe asthma and non-asthma donors
model_systems.culture_system: air-liquid-interface culture with optional microfluidic airway-chip format

perturbations.name: IL-13 type 2 cytokine exposure and withdrawal
perturbations.description: Timed IL-13 stimulation followed by withdrawal to induce and then test resolution of type 2 mucous metaplasia.

perturbations.name: MTOR pathway inhibition
perturbations.description: Rapamycin or matched MTOR-pathway perturbation used to test whether epithelial growth and migration programs maintain mucous-cell remodeling.

readouts.name: MUC5AC mucous metaplasia
readouts.description: MUC5AC-positive goblet-cell abundance and mucin secretion after IL-13 exposure, cytokine withdrawal, and MTOR inhibition.

readouts.name: Basal-to-apical epithelial migration and proliferation
readouts.description: BrdU/Ki-67 and spatial-position readouts that test whether mucous metaplasia is coupled to epithelial proliferation and migration.

readouts.name: Epithelial-state resolution
readouts.description: Single-cell transcriptomic recovery of basal, secretory, goblet, and ciliated epithelial-state proportions after cytokine withdrawal.

controls.name: Non-asthma donor airway epithelium
controls.description: Matched epithelial cultures from donors without asthma.

controls.name: Vehicle-treated airway epithelium
controls.description: Air-liquid-interface cultures receiving vehicle rather than IL-13 or MTOR inhibitor.

assertion.decision_criterion: A persistent epithelial knowledge gap is resolved if a mucous-cell state remains after IL-13 withdrawal in severe-asthma cultures and is reduced by MTOR inhibition along with proliferation or migration readouts. Reversibility is supported if withdrawal alone restores epithelial-state proportions and MUC5AC secretion to non-asthma control ranges.

selected_evidence.snippet: Airways from individuals with severe asthma showed increased MTOR signaling by RPS6 phosphorylation

assertion.hypothesis_label: Amplification of polygenic asthma risk in adverse contexts via shared airway-inflammation convergence
assertion.description: Polygenic-score-by-context (PGS×C) interactions reported for asthma in the UK Biobank appear to reflect amplification rather than context-specific causal variants: the same susceptibility loci (e.g. IL4, IL13, HLA-DQ, CDHR3) exert systematically larger effects in disease-promoting contexts. This entry proposes that the amplification arises because polygenic liability and adverse exposures — tobacco smoke, air pollution and allergen load — converge on the shared Airway Inflammation node, so their joint effect on the liability-threshold scale is super-additive rather than additive. Nagpal & Gibson (Nat Genet 2026, PMID:42443528) include asthma among the seven diseases showing pervasive PGS×context interactions in the UK Biobank.
assertion.notes: EMERGING hypothesis motivated by population-scale PGS×context analyses (primary source PMID:42443528; general amplification mechanism corroborated by PMID:37228747). The convergence claim (polygenic liability + adverse exposures → Airway Inflammation) is a mechanistic interpretation and is not itself established as causal — see the reverse-causation knowledge gap under discussions.

selected_evidence.snippet: GxSex is pervasive but acts primarily through systematic sex differences in the magnitude of many genetic effects

Oral corticosteroids are the cornerstone of management of acute moderate or severe asthma whilst preventive inhaled corticosteroids are the mainstay of the preventive management of children with asthma. Yet, variation in the magnitude of response to corticosteroids has been observed.

assertion.name: Hill mechanochemical morphoelastic model of asthmatic airway remodelling
assertion.description: Axisymmetric continuum model coupling transient inflammatory or contractile agonist challenges, airway-smooth-muscle contraction, mechanical stress, mechanotransductive agonist release, and long-term growth of smooth muscle and extracellular matrix in a nonlinear fibre-reinforced airway wall.
assertion.model_format: Coupled mechanochemical continuum and morphoelastic equations

modeled_mechanisms.description: Simulates long-term changes in airway-smooth-muscle and extracellular-matrix volume produced by repeated inflammatory and contractile challenges.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The airway is an idealized axisymmetric elastic cylinder rather than a patient-specific bronchial tree, and parameter combinations were explored theoretically rather than prospectively fitted to human longitudinal data.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Couples local agonist concentration to smooth-muscle contraction and predicts persistent contractile tone through mechanotransductive feedback.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Airflow, heterogeneous airway branching, neural control, mucus obstruction, and whole-lung ventilation are outside the single-airway-wall formulation.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Represents transient inflammatory challenges and their clearance as model inputs that initiate remodelling and contraction feedback.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Inflammation is reduced to agonist and mediator fields; immune-cell recruitment, asthma endotypes, and cytokine-specific signaling are not represented explicitly.

variables.name: Airway smooth muscle volume fraction
variables.description: Local fraction of airway-wall tissue occupied by smooth muscle

variables.name: Extracellular matrix volume fraction
variables.description: Local fraction of airway-wall tissue occupied by extracellular matrix

variables.name: Contractile agonist concentration
variables.description: Local contractile stimulus controlling smooth-muscle activation

variables.name: Mitogenic mediator concentration
variables.description: Local pro-growth signal controlling constituent remodelling

variables.name: Airway lumen radius
variables.description: Inner airway-wall radius during growth and active contraction

findings.statement: Mechanical stress generated by smooth-muscle contraction created a positive feedback loop that increased remodelling in hyper-responsive simulated airways.
Persistent contractile tone emerged when feedback was pathological, agonist clearance failed, or both conditions occurred together.

assertion.notes: Curated from the article and equations; no deposited executable implementation was identified. This is a theoretical airway-wall model, not a patient-specific digital twin or a clinical predictor.

selected_evidence.snippet: In order to obtain a better understanding of their inter-dependence, we develop a mechanochemical morphoelastic model of the airway wall accounting for local volume changes in airway smooth muscle (ASM) and extracellular matrix in response to transient inflammatory or contractile agonist challenges.
